name: chemical-engineering
statement: I want to learn chemical engineering

nodes.name: Units and dimensional consistency
misconceptions: treats mol and kg as interchangeable

nodes.name: Mass and molar flow, molecular weight conversion
misconceptions: confuses mass fraction with mole fraction

nodes.name: Process flowsheets and degrees of freedom
Steady-state mass balance on a single unit
misconceptions: includes accumulation term at steady state

nodes.name: Multi-unit balances with recycle
misconceptions: balances recycle loop as if it were the overall system

nodes.name: Stoichiometry, extent of reaction, limiting reactant
misconceptions: picks limiting reactant by smallest mass

nodes.name: Reactive systems balances with recycle and purge

families.stem: Convert {q} lbm/h to kg/s.
A classmate writes 3 kg + 2 mol = 5. Explain what went wrong and what would be needed to combine them.
families.key: units differ; need molecular weight to convert

families.stem: A recipe needs {q} cups of water per batch; the plant meters water in L/min at {r} batches per hour. What flow is that?
A stream carries {m} kg/h of methanol (MW 32.04). What is the molar flow in kmol/h?
A gas is 30 mol% CO2 (MW 44) and 70 mol% N2 (MW 28). What is the CO2 mass fraction?
Fill in: moles = mass / ____.
A mixer has two feeds and one product, three components, all feed flows and compositions known. How many degrees of freedom remain for the product?
Why is a mass fraction you were given not an unknown in a degree-of-freedom count, while one you were not given is?
families.key: specified values are known; unknowns are unspecified variables

families.stem: {f} kg/h of 40% ethanol is distilled. The top is 90% ethanol and the bottom 5%. Find the top flow at steady state.
A student writes in - out = accumulation for a continuous column running for months, and leaves accumulation unknown. What would you tell them?
families.key: steady state means accumulation is zero

families.stem: Water (1.00 kg/L) and oil (0.85 kg/L) are mixed at {a} L/min and {b} L/min. What is the product mass flow?
Hint: total in = total out. A splitter takes {f} kg/h and sends 30% to stream B. What is stream A?
A coffee shop blends {x} kg/day of beans at 12% moisture with dry beans to reach 8%. How much dry bean is needed?
A dryer with recycle: fresh feed {f} kg/h at 20% water joins a recycle stream; the dryer product is 2% water. Find the overall product flow.
Your partner starts the recycle problem by balancing around the mixing point and gets stuck with too many unknowns. Where should they draw the first boundary and why?
families.key: overall system boundary first; recycle cancels

families.stem: A city water loop: {f} m3/h of fresh water, 60% of the treated water is recirculated. Find the discharge at steady state.
N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3. Feed is {a} g N2 and {b} g H2. Which reactant limits?
C3H8 + 5O2 -> 3CO2 + 4H2O. With {n} mol propane at 80% conversion, how many mol O2 are consumed?
Explain what extent of reaction measures and why it is the same no matter which species you compute it from.
Ammonia synthesis with recycle and a purge of {p}% of the recycle gas; inert argon enters at 0.2% of fresh feed. Find the purge rate that keeps argon at 5% in the recycle.
Why does a recycle loop with an inert in the feed need a purge, and what happens without one?
families.key: inert accumulates without an exit; steady state impossible

families.stem: A brewery recycles CO2 scrubbing water; dissolved salts enter at {s} ppm. With a {p}% blowdown, find the steady salt level.
